title: Alibi and Will
premise: Sable Crane, the famously discreet concierge of the Grand Meridian Hotel, receives a confession letter postmarked one day after the funeral of hotel owner Augustin Voss—signed by a guest who died three years ago. As Sable investigates, they uncover a coded ledger woven into the hotel's own architecture that documents Voss's blackmail empire, implicating staff Sable has considered family for a decade. The letter was sent by Voss's daughter, who faked her death to escape him and now needs Sable to expose the ledger before the statute of limitations shields the guilty. In the end, Sable must choose between protecting the loyal colleagues who enabled Voss and publishing the truth, ultimately decoding the ledger publicly while quietly arranging escape for those who were victims first.
about_author: Edmund Ravensworth is the pen name of a former night auditor at a grand European hotel who spent twenty years listening at the edge of other people's secrets. He writes mysteries from a coastal cottage, insisting that every lobby is a confession booth with better lighting.

chapters.title: The Day After Forever
chapters.summary: Sable Crane's POV. Three days after Augustin Voss's lavish funeral, Sable sorts the dead man's forwarded mail and finds a confession letter postmarked the day after the burial—signed by Elodie Voss, who drowned three years ago. The beat is quiet dread: the invisible concierge realizes someone has finally seen them.

chapters.title: A Concierge's Memory
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with flashbacks. Establishing Sable's gift: they remember every guest, favor, and lie that passed through the Meridian's lobby. They recall Elodie's 'drowning' weekend in suspicious detail—a closed wing, a doctored register. Emotional beat: pride curdling into complicity as Sable admits what they chose not to see.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following a hint in the letter—'he kept his sins where everyone could admire them'—Sable notices the lobby's decorative frieze repeats an odd numerical motif. They photograph it and begin mapping dates against old reservation books. Beat: the thrill of the hunt rekindling a conscience long dormant.

chapters.title: Grief Wears Good Tailoring
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marcus Hale, Voss's lawyer and executor, reading the will. Voss leaves everything to a trust controlled by Hale, with a strange clause: the hotel cannot be sold for five years. Hale burns a page before the family arrives. Beat: cold ambition; the reader learns the will itself is a weapon.

chapters.title: The Staff Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable quietly interviews longtime staff—housekeeper Marta, bartender Dev, night manager Ivo—and finds each deflects when Elodie's name surfaces. Their loyalty to Voss ran deeper than wages. Beat: belonging as a cage; Sable loves these people and begins to fear them.

chapters.title: Postmark Ghost
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, revealed through her letters. She narrates her staged death: Voss discovered she'd copied his ledger and gave her a choice—the water or exile under a new name. She chose neither cleanly. Beat: terror and defiance; the 'confession' is actually a summons.

chapters.title: Room 412 Never Slept
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Records show Room 412 was occupied the week after Elodie's death by a guest who never checked out properly—paid in cash, registered under a name Sable now recognizes as an anagram. Someone helped her vanish from inside the hotel. Beat: hope that an ally exists, shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Hale's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale's POV. Hale discovers someone has been querying the archives and starts his own count—not of crimes, but of witnesses still employed. He offers Sable a promotion designed to buy silence. Beat: corruption offered politely, power as currency; Sable declines without saying no.

chapters.title: The Frieze Speaks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Late-night work cracks the cipher: the frieze numbers map to dates, room numbers, and initials—a twenty-year record of payments, threats, and favors. Several initials belong to beloved colleagues. Beat: heartbreak; the ledger indicts the family Sable built.

chapters.title: Marta's Hands
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The housekeeper remembers laundering money through linen invoices to pay for her son's surgery, believing Voss was 'generous.' She senses Sable knows. Beat: guilt and gratitude tangled; loyalty to a monster because he paid for love.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A retired detective warns Sable: key charges expire in six weeks, and Hale is already maneuvering to have records sealed with the estate. The clock becomes the plot's engine. Beat: urgency; truth has a deadline, and lawyers are faster than consciences.

chapters.title: The Anagram Guest
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable traces the alias to Ivo, the night manager, who covered Elodie's escape. Confronted in the wine cellar, Ivo confesses—but reveals he also kept copying the ledger for insurance, and someone stole his copy last month. Beat: alliance formed under threat; paranoia deepens.

chapters.title: What the Will Withholds
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale's POV. Hale finds Voss's private addendum: proof that Voss intended to disinherit Hale and expose him as the embezzler behind two 'guest' deaths. Hale realizes he isn't the heir—he's the next defendant. Beat: panic beneath polish; the corrupt turn on each other.

chapters.title: Fire Drill at Midnight
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A small fire in the archive room destroys a decade of registers. Arson, obviously—but Sable had photographed the crucial pages. Now whoever set it knows Sable has them. Beat: escalation; the investigation turns physical and dangerous.

chapters.title: Dev Pours One Out
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The bartender, who laundered Voss's cash unknowingly at first, then knowingly, decides to talk to Sable after nearly being run down by a black sedan. His testimony links Hale to the intimidation campaign. Beat: courage from the least likely; solidarity forming among the small people.

chapters.title: Elodie Comes Home
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She returns disguised as a consultant for the estate appraisal, testing whether Sable can be trusted face-to-face. Their lobby conversation—two watchers recognizing each other—is the book's quiet centerpiece. Beat: wary intimacy; the ghost becomes a person.

chapters.title: The Trust Clause Trap
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Decoding the will clause, Sable realizes the five-year lock exists so Hale can legally destroy the ledger once limitations expire—the hotel itself would swallow the evidence. They have weeks, not years. Beat: despair into resolve; the building Sable loves is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Every Initial Named
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating short POVs (Marta, Dev, Ivo, Elodie). Each implicated staffer chooses, independently, to stand with Sable rather than Hale—some for redemption, some for revenge. Beat: belonging redefined; loyalty redirected from power to truth.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the formal will reading, Hale announces the estate's 'orderly dissolution' plan. Sable publicly presents the decoded frieze and the stolen-copy theft, forcing the executor to respond on the record before witnesses and a journalist Dev invited. Beat: climax; invisibility abandoned on purpose.

chapters.title: Hale Unbound
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale's POV. Cornered, Hale attempts to burn the frieze itself and take Elodie hostage as leverage, revealing he knew about her survival all along—he helped Voss stage it. Sable and Ivo intervene; staff seal the exits. Beat: violence erupting in the gilded lobby; power exposed as desperation.

chapters.title: Testimony Before Expiry
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With hours before the statute closes, statements are filed: Marta's invoices, Dev's testimony, Ivo's copy, Elodie alive and sworn. Charges land on Hale and the estate; protections are negotiated for the coerced staff. Beat: catharsis; justice arriving not clean, but on time.

chapters.title: Concierge, Still
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue. Months later, the Meridian reopens under staff ownership with Elodie as silent partner. Sable keeps the desk, keeps the memory, and mails one last letter—to the person who taught them that noticing everything means answering for it. Beat: belonging earned; the watcher finally seen, and at peace.
